Subject: SOC 2 scope: non-prod & dedicated pools eligibility

Hi Irene,

We’re preparing FinBank’s SOC request package and have a couple of scope questions about Redwood’s Type II coverage we hope you can confirm quickly:

1) Does Redwood’s SOC 2 Type II report (the most recent period) cover non-production environments (staging/preview) for customers using the hosted API, or is it limited to production endpoints only?

2) For customers on Dedicated (reserved GPU pools), if a customer has both production and staging workloads running in the same dedicated pool, are those non-prod instances covered by Redwood’s assessment (assuming the pool is isolated to the customer)?

3) For Private/VPC/on-prem deployments where the customer manages the control plane (we deploy a package into the customer VPC), are those instances considered in-scope for Redwood’s SOC 2, or would FinBank need to rely on our own attestation for those environments?

Also: FinBank’s auditors are asking for a bridge-letter to cover the audit period Oct 1, 2025 – Mar 31, 2026 (the period overlaps a previous Redwood Type II). Can you confirm whether Redwood can provide a signed bridge letter to: (a) confirm what hosting modes were included in that period, and (b) identify any known control changes that would affect scope/backfill?

Finally, please point me to the artifacts you can share (tenant isolation/topology diagrams, evidence mapping to controls, KMS ownership details, and any contractual identifier we can include in the report).

Thanks — we’re aiming to share the finalized package with auditors by next Thursday (9/2). Any chance you can reply with a short scope statement and an ETA for the bridge letter?

Best,
Alex Mercer
Head of Security Operations
FinBank

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: SOC 2 scope: non-prod & dedicated pools eligibility

Alex — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, followed by details and next steps.

Short answers:
- Hosted (Redwood-managed) API: scope in our Type II is scoped to production endpoints that were exercised in the test period. Non-production (customer staging/preview) endpoints hosted on our multi-tenant platform are typically excluded unless specifically covered by an explicit, contractually-isolated environment that was included in the audit evidence.
- Dedicated (reserved GPU pools): if the dedicated pool is provisioned and configured as customer-isolated (no shared tenants) and that pool was identified to the auditors as in-scope during the assessment, those pools are covered — both prod and non-prod instances within that isolated pool can be considered in-scope provided the customer’s non-prod workloads run inside the same isolated tenancy that was evaluated.
- Private / VPC / on-prem: when customers run our Private package and operate the control plane (customer-managed), those environments are out of scope for Redwood’s SOC 2 because the audited controls are not exercised by Redwood. For customers using Redwood-managed VPC control planes (Redwood-hosted control plane into a customer VPC), we can evaluate coverage on a case-by-case basis — please identify the deployment model and the contract name.

Bridge letter & artifacts:
- We can provide a bridge letter for Oct 1, 2025 – Mar 31, 2026 that: (a) states which hosting modes were considered in the Type II report period, (b) confirms any control changes materially affecting scope during that period, and (c) references the relevant report and testing window.
- Attaching a short summary and example artifacts now: redwood_soc2_summary_2024-2026.pdf and a ZIP of recent audit artifacts can be pulled on request.

Next steps/proposed timeline:
1) I’ll connect this thread to our compliance owners and request a draft bridge letter.
2) Please confirm whether FinBank’s staging workloads are running in a customer-isolated Dedicated pool, or on our shared hosted endpoints (you can send the pool id or contract number). If you provide the dedicated pool id I’ll ask Marcus to confirm it was included in the audited inventory.
3) We can schedule a 30-min touch with auditors if they want more color.

I’ll follow up with a draft bridge letter within 48 business hours once Marcus confirms the dedicated-pool mapping.

- Irene
Irene Choi
Principal, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
